root_idea.summary: The root centers on safety, soundness, and freedom from harm, and extends to peace, reconciliation, and willing submission.
root_idea.development: From the basic idea of being safe and sound come meanings of securing or saving, making peace, submitting or entering into Islam, and related uses such as advance delivery and a ladder as a means of reaching a safe destination.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Normalized to the masculine singular passive-participle citation form.
Normalized to the singular active-participle citation form.
Normalized from the prefixed Quranic form to the lexical noun سَلْم.
Quranic vocalic/formal variant of the noun سِلْم, used for peace or Islam.

senses.definition: to make safe, secure, or free from harm; to save or preserve
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use, including God's saving or securing someone from danger.

senses.definition: to greet or salute someone with a prayer or declaration of peace
senses.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَى and related greeting constructions; the greeting invokes safety and freedom from harm.

senses.definition: to deliver, hand over, or pay something to its recipient
senses.usage_conditions: Used with إِلَى or an expressed recipient; includes handing over property or a required payment.

senses.definition: to submit, assent, or yield without opposition
senses.usage_conditions: Used of accepting a command, decree, judgment, or established truth; this is distinct from physically handing something over.

senses.definition: to submit or resign oneself to God; to become obedient and submissive
senses.usage_conditions: In religious usage, the verb can denote entering or professing Islam; in fuller usage it includes inward assent and obedient submission, with the object often understood or expressed with لِ.

senses.definition: submission to God and adherence to the religion of Islam
senses.usage_conditions: As a legal or theological term, it may refer to outward profession and religious affiliation; in its fuller use it includes belief, obedient action, and resignation to God's decree.

senses.definition: one who submits to God; a Muslim, submissive or obedient to Him
senses.usage_conditions: The active participle functions adjectivally and substantivally, in masculine, feminine, singular, dual, and plural forms; it can describe religious identity or the state of submission itself.

senses.definition: one who surrenders or is wholly submissive
senses.usage_conditions: The Form X active participle emphasizes entering or remaining in a state of surrender.

senses.definition: delivered or handed over as a required payment
senses.usage_conditions: In the compensation construction, the item or payment is something to be delivered to its rightful recipient.

senses.definition: sound, intact, and free from visible blemish
senses.usage_conditions: Describes an object that has been made acceptable by being free of external defect; the Quranic example concerns an animal without markings or blemish.

senses.definition: sound, safe, or free from defect
senses.usage_conditions: An active-participle adjective describing a state of soundness or freedom from harm.

senses.definition: safety, security, peace, or freedom from harm and defect
senses.usage_conditions: Includes peaceful safety, safe arrival, and the Quranic expressions دار السلام and سبل السلام. By extension, السَّلَام is a divine name or epithet denoting freedom from imperfection and the giver of safety.

senses.definition: a salutation or greeting invoking peace and safety
senses.usage_conditions: Used in formulas such as سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكَ or سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ, and in the reciprocal greeting of visitors or believers.

senses.definition: a declaration of disengagement: no harm, conflict, or further involvement between the parties
senses.usage_conditions: In the construction وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ قَالُوا سَلَامًا, the word is interpreted as withdrawing from altercation rather than offering the ordinary greeting.

senses.definition: peace, reconciliation, or a state of submission
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a noun or verbal noun for peaceable submission and the absence of resistance.

senses.definition: exclusive submission or allegiance to one master or party
senses.usage_conditions: In the construction of a person belonging or submitting exclusively to one master, it contrasts with divided association among several masters.

senses.definition: sound, whole, and free from inner corruption or defect
senses.usage_conditions: In بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ, the adjective describes a heart free from unbelief, spiritual corruption, or unsoundness.

senses.definition: a ladder, stairway, or means of ascending
senses.usage_conditions: The noun may denote a physical ladder or stairway and, by extension, a means of reaching a higher place or goal.

senses.definition: peace or reconciliation
senses.usage_conditions: A noun for peace in contrast with war, including entering into a peaceful settlement.

senses.definition: peace, reconciliation, or submission
senses.usage_conditions: The word is used for peace in opposition to war and can also denote self-resignation or submission.

senses.definition: Islam, understood as submission and obedience to God
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction ادْخُلُوا فِي السِّلْمِ, the noun is interpreted as the religion or comprehensive state of submission.

senses.definition: submission, assent, or complete yielding
senses.usage_conditions: The verbal noun denotes accepting a judgment or command without resistance, including complete submission in a legal or religious context.

senses.definition: salutation or greeting
senses.usage_conditions: As the verbal noun of سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ, it denotes offering a greeting or salutational prayer for peace.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to be free or clear of participation, encumbrance, or claim; to belong exclusively to someone
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use for a property or possession becoming free of another person's participation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to make someone captive
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare transitive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: for a serpent to bite someone
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Rarely attested lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to tan a hide with the leaves of the salām tree
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized craft use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to finish making a leather bucket and make it firm or sound
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use concerning manufacture of a leather bucket.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to abandon, forsake, or leave someone exposed to harm or destruction
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of leaving a person or enemy without aid, or giving him over to a harmful fate.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to entrust or commit one's case to God
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction with the matter or case as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to acknowledge or concede the truth or justice of a claim
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A legal or argumentative use derived from the idea of yielding something to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to pay or deliver a price in advance
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A commercial construction in which the commodity is to be delivered later according to description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to leave or abandon an affair after having been engaged in it
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A non-religious use with عَنْهُ or an understood object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to declare oneself free, clear, or quit of something or someone
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive Form V use with مِنْهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to take or receive something delivered
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of receiving a thing that has been given or handed over.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to make peace or reconcile with one another
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to agree or correspond with one another; figuratively, for statements or movements to be consistent
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative use is applied to two troops keeping pace or to assertions agreeing with one another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to become reconciled or at peace
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare Form VIII use during or after displeasure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to touch, stroke, wipe, kiss, or reach the Black Stone
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A ritual construction concerning contact with the Black Stone of the Kaaba, by hand or with a staff.

other_classical_meanings.definition: for a crop to put forth its ears
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: for a boot to soften or make the feet tender
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use concerning footwear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to proceed along the middle or straight course of a road without missing it
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized directional use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to call or name oneself a Muslim
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexicalized Form II of the special-form family.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a leather bucket with one handle or loop
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun distinct from the peace noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a sale in which the price is paid in advance for a described commodity delivered later
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The commercial transaction also called advance payment or salam sale.

other_classical_meanings.definition: the taking or state of a captive without resistance
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Can describe bringing someone captive or submissive, including without a fight or while wounded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: stones, especially hard stones; also a broad stone
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective or plural-like noun with varying accounts of its singular.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a woman soft or tender in the extremities
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive noun for bodily softness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: an old and weak she-camel
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a plant that becomes green in the season of summer or spring
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a gecko or related lizard
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional zoological designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: the earth or ground in a proverbial expression
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported reading is associated with a proverb and is distinct from the more common wording.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a household's intimate or special friend, one who mixes closely with it
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression based on the name Salmān.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a kind of black beetle
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A zoological noun, with several reported identifications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a plural or quasi-plural term for salām trees or stones
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The interpretation varies with the reading and context of the transmitted expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a kind of tree, or a single salām tree
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical use distinct from the abstract noun of safety.

other_classical_meanings.definition: one bitten by a serpent; by extension, wounded or near death
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The apparently positive form is explained as an auspicious name or as one left exposed to the poison within him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: the interior or specified part of a horse's hoof
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equine anatomical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a small bone, especially a phalanx or the small bones of the fingers, toes, hand, or foot
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun has several anatomical applications to human and animal bones.

other_classical_meanings.definition: the south or southerly wind
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a kind of tree growing in soft or plain tracts
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: red ants
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional zoological expression, literally “the ants of Solomon.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: a group of stars likened to a ladder
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative astronomical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a stirrup or means of mounting
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extension from the ladder as an aid to ascent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a means or avenue leading to another thing
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on reaching a destination by ascending a ladder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: the name of a particular horse
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a good, well-formed, or unobjectionable word or expression
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of a word or sentence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: the leaves of the doum palm
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical use unrelated to the comparative adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: the collective body of Muslims
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective use in expressions such as أهل الإسلام.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Islamic; pertaining or relating to Islam
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival derivative of الإِسْلَام.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a poet of the early Islamic-era class following the mukhadramūn and preceding the later muwalladūn
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical classification in literary history.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a word or phrase given a new technical sense through the promulgation of Islam
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A term in discussions of religiously introduced usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a vein in the hand between the little finger and the adjacent finger
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is attested only in the diminutive form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: touched or kissed, especially in reference to the Black Stone
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare passive-participle use connected with the ritual verb اِسْتَلَمَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a hide or skin tanned with salām-tree leaves
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun of craft and tanning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: land abounding in salām trees
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective descriptive formation for a tract containing many such trees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a man soft or tender in the feet
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized bodily description.

cautions: The QAC groups السَّلْم and السِّلْم separately by vocalization; the latter is presented as سِلْم while the former is presented as سَلْم, with the transmitted Quranic readings retained through their form-group accounting.
Some Lane Quran references use historical chapter-and-verse notation; no such citation has been converted into a modern verse location unless the corresponding QAC location is supplied.
The public headword مُسَلَّم is normalized from the Quranic feminine passive participle مُسَلَّمَة, while feminine and plural active-participle forms are grouped under مُسْلِم.
